title: Incremental refactor review capture - backlog to PR notes
content:
Purpose:
Quick capture of my running thoughts while reviewing the incremental refactor PR (PR #2147). This is messy — notes for follow-ups, small TODOs to add to the PR, and a short test plan. Save before I forget.

High-level summary:
- PR attempts to break up large request_dispatcher.go into request_router + handler pipeline pieces.
- Adds an explicit batching interface and a small KV-cache coherence shim.
- Introduces a FeatureFlag to enable new route sharding (experimental).

Immediate concerns (blocking-ish):
- KV-cache race on evict: cache.incrEvict() uses map iteration without lock during concurrent read from Serve(). I flagged line ~297 in cache.go. Either add RWMutex or switch to sync.Map for now.
- Benchmark regression potential: the new batching interface adds an indirection layer; need microbench before/after for short sequences (seq_len <= 32). Put a perf job on perf infra.
- Error wrapping: several errors are returned as strings (fmt.Errorf("err: %v", e)). Standardize to errors.Wrap or use github.com/pkg/errors to preserve stack. Not critical but tech debt.

Suggested inline fixes (small):
- request_router.go: replace for-loop with for idx, r := range reqs { ... } to avoid accidental mutation of r when passed to goroutines.
- batching/batcher_test.go: add deterministic test with fake clock to avoid flakiness (current TestBatchFlush sometimes times out on CI).
- Add a simple integration test hitting the canary route sharding flag: integration/canary-route-smoke.go (just one request, assert routed node id).

Follow-ups (create tickets or PR comments):
- FR1: Add a perf benchmark: bench/bench_batch_sequence_test.go with sequences {8,16,32,128} and measure p50/p95 token latency. Attach results to PR. (Assigned to me)
- FR2: Lock KV cache or migrate to sync.Map + add a race-test (go test -race) in CI gating. (Blocker)
- FR3: Add Telemetry: expose histogram for batching wait time and queue depth. Minimal: prometheus metric name "batcher_queue_depth".

Testing checklist (for merge):
- [ ] Unit tests pass locally (make test): serving-runtime unit suite (currently 1521 tests)
- [ ] go test -race on batching + cache packages
- [ ] Run perf job w/ small sequences and compare to baseline (attach numbers in PR comment)
- [ ] End-to-end smoke: deploy to staging with feature flag on + run 100 concurrent short requests, ensure no 5xx and avg latency < 120ms
- [ ] Canary rollout plan noted in PR: 5% -> 20% -> 100% over 4 hours with manual stop on errors > 0.5%

Rollout / rollback criteria (quick):
- Quick stop if errors spike > 0.5% or p95 latency increases by > 40% relative to baseline.
- If memory spikes > 20% on serving nodes, rollback immediately.

Notes to self (written raw):
- Could simplify handler pipeline by moving metric emission earlier so each stage reads from context rather than re-wrapping. Might reduce allocations.
- Consider making batching interface generic over request type with type params (Go 1.20+?). Might be overkill.
- Revisit naming: request_dispatcher -> request_coordinator felt clearer but keep for now.

Slack signals / related threads:
- Priya mentioned in #serving-runtime earlier about flaky tests on CI after isolating the batching change. Follow up with her for exact failing job IDs.

PR comment draft (short):
Thanks for the clean split — big +1 for modularization. I left a few inline suggestions re: cache locking and a perf benchmark request. Before merging I'd like a focused perf run and a race-test added. Once green, we can canary with 5% traffic per the rollout plan.

Action items (me):
- [ ] Add bench + attach numbers to PR (due 2026-03-12)
- [ ] Draft PR comment + request Priya to run flaky CI job
- [ ] Create JIRA for KV-cache race if we don't patch in PR

Random scratchpad ideas (non-blocking):
- If batching wait-time metric is high on warm nodes, add "fast-path" that bypasses queue for single-request latency-sensitive calls.
- Might be worth a short doc recording "serving-runtime refactor guidelines" (one-pager) to keep future splits consistent.

End.
